1.2.3.14-r1.burton_quote: He hath scorned all money, bribes, gifts, upright otherwise and sincere, hath inserted himself to no fond Imagination, and sustained all those tyrannical concupiscences of the body, hath lost all his honour, captivated by vainglory

1.2.3.14-r11.burton_quote: Cotys King of Thrace, was married to Minerva, and sent three several messengers one after another, to see if she were come to his bedchamber

1.2.3.14-r13.burton_quote: a Smith of Milan, a fellow Citizen of his, one Galeus de Rubeis, that being commended for refinding of an instrument of Archimedes, for joy ran mad

1.2.3.14-r14.burton_quote: grew thereupon so arrogant, that in a short space after he lost his wits

1.2.3.14-r15.burton_quote: came abroad all squalid and submiss, and gave no other reason to his friends of so doing, than that he perceived himself the day before, by reason of his good fortune, to be too insolent, overmuch joyed

1.2.3.14-r2.burton_quote: insomuch as those that are misaffected with it, never so much as once perceive it, or think of any cure

1.2.3.14-r3.burton_quote: I cannot express how pleasing it is to me to hear myself commended

1.2.3.14-r6.burton_quote: There was never yet true Poet nor Orator, that thought any other better than himself

1.2.3.14-r7.burton_quote: cannot endure to be contradicted, or hear of anything but their own commendation
